report.summary: Multi-agent orchestration shows mixed results. On SWE-bench, single-agent systems like SWE-agent (12.3% resolve) and Devin (13.8%) outperform many multi-agent frameworks (e.g., MetaGPT ~8%). However, specialized multi-agent designs like ChatDev (14.9% on SWE-bench-lite) and AutoGen's role-playing (e.g., code reviewer + coder) can exceed single agents on complex tasks. Fan-out helps when tasks require diverse expertise (e.g., software design, code review) but hurts on well-defined, sequential tasks due to coordination overhead and error propagation. Key benchmarks: SWE-bench (single-agent leads
risks: Coordination overhead can degrade performance on simple tasks.
Error propagation between agents can amplify mistakes.
Increased latency and cost without guaranteed improvement.
todos: Benchmark on your specific task domain before committing to multi-agent.
Consider hybrid: single agent with selective multi-agent subroutines.
Measure coordination cost (tokens, time) vs. accuracy gain.

handoff.suggestion: Run a controlled experiment: compare a single strong agent (e.g., GPT-4 with ReAct) against a multi-agent system (e.g., AutoGen with coder+reviewer) on a representative subset of your tasks. Report resolve rate, cost, and latency.
